head: 022dc11
summary: Structural Phase 4 work is solid. All 12 implementer commits land cleanly: Tier 3 gates produce the exact required compile-error message format, gated widgets compile under their flags, WithWebFallback companions cross-compile on web / iOS / macOS, the Platform.requires macro works, tier-matrix.md classifies every widget, CLAUDE.md additions are scoped, Crystal spec suite shows 4 pre-existing baseline failures + zero new failures, Swift tests 53/53 PASS, iOS XCUITest Phase 3 behavior suite 10/10 PASS. Three deviations the implementer self-disclosed are verified as architecturally sound. FAIL is driven by unverified web-fallback behavior checks (focus trap / Escape / axe-core / IBM Equal Access / positioning / touch targets) — these require a CDP-driven headless-Chrome harness and no pre-built Phase 4 demo test page exists; the JS source inspection confirms the implementation logic is present but the rubric explicitly states these checks 'do NOT pass on source inspection.' macOS AXTest BX2/BX7 also fail, but this is reproduced on the cda36b2 baseline so it is NOT a Phase 4 regression — it is a pre-existing environmental/TCC issue.

architect_attention.item: Web fallback behavior verification deferred — no test page exists
architect_attention.detail: The 11 'fallback.*-axe-clean / fallback.*-ibm-* / focus.* / conformance.*' checks all require a CDP-driven headless-Chrome run against a live rendered test page. No samples/web/phase04_*.html test page exists in the repo. The rubric explicitly forbids source-only verdicts on these checks. JS source inspection shows the implementation logic is present and structurally sound (focus trap, Escape handler, ARIA roles, positioning math, touch-target classes), but conformance to the rubric requires a real-page check. RECOMMENDATION: implementer adds 3 web test pages (action sheet presented, context menu trigger trio at TL/center/BR, breadcrumb path control) and a CDP harness script following docs/initiative-cross-platform-ui/rubric/behavior-simulation-toolkit.md, then re-runs validation.

architect_attention.item: macOS AXTest BX2/BX7 fail on both Phase 4 HEAD and cda36b2 baseline
architect_attention.detail: Not a Phase 4 regression. The hig_showcase binary launches and prints RECT_PX confirming the window mounts, but the AX query for 'tap-probe-button' returns nil on both branches. The same specs were green in phase-03-evidence-2026-05-21-iter5. Likely root cause: ad-hoc re-signing the binary invalidates TCC Accessibility grants (the Makefile comment notes this explicitly: 'TCC permissions persist across rebuilds ONLY if the binary is signed with a stable identity'). Codesign identity 'Developer ID Application: AgentC Consulting LLC (PXDF92M2T4)' is set, so the binary IS being signed with a stable identity — but if the developer manually edited any binary recently the grant could have been invalidated. Re-granting Accessibility in System Settings to the new binary path should restore. This is a pre-existing flakiness in the test environment, not a code regression.
